facts.statement: Bavaricarbo is an extinct genus of cormorant from the Miocene of Germany.
facts.quote: Bavaricarbo is an extinct genus of cormorant (family Phalacrocoracidae) from the Miocene Hammerschmiede clay pit, Germany.

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Bavaricarbo is B. brevirostris.
facts.quote: The type species is B. brevirostris.

facts.statement: The type locality for Bavaricarbo is the Hammerschmiede clay pit.
Bavaricarbo was described by Mayr, Lechner, and Böhme.
Bavaricarbo lived during the Miocene epoch.
The description of Bavaricarbo was published in the Swiss Journal of Palaeontology.
Bavaricarbo is classified as a member of the stem group of the cormorant family Phalacrocoracidae.
facts.quote: A member of the stem group of Phalacrocoracidae.

facts.statement: Bavaricarbo fossils date to the early Late Miocene (earliest Tortonian) from the Hammerschmiede clay pit in southern Germany.
The presence of Bavaricarbo and other piscivorous birds suggests the Hammerschmiede site had a highly productive river system with ample prey.
